text: Every October, farmers in Punjab have about three weeks between harvesting rice and sowing wheat.
Straw still on the field gets burned, and the smoke reaches every village and city downwind.
The machines that clear straw without fire already exist.
What is missing is a plan: the right machine, on the right field, on the right day.
StrawLink is that plan.
This is one block near Sangrur: two hundred paddy fields, real roads, and three plants that take straw.
Gold fields are harvested and waiting. Green fields are still standing.
Press run, and today's plan plays out.
Baler sets bale the straw.
Trucks carry the bales to a plant that still has room.
Where the plants are full, a Super Seeder sows wheat straight through the straw.
The scoreboard counts fields cleared, straw handled, and whether this fleet can finish before the sowing deadline.
Nothing here is scripted. Every slider asks the real planner, running on AWS.
say: Nothing here is scripted. Every slider asks the real planner, running on A W S.

text: Double the baler sets, and nothing improves, because every truck trip is already used.
Add trucks and seeders too, and the same day clears twice as many fields.
Now an officer knows which machine to hire, before spending a single rupee.
Add rain, and the planner keeps machines off wet fields until they dry.
Satellite images show each field turning from green to gold, and a model forecasts every harvest date.
Click any field to see when its machine comes, and why.
Farmers need no app. They ask on WhatsApp, in Punjabi.
An assistant on Amazon Bedrock answers, using only the current plan.
A harvest date from the farmer overrides the satellite, and the day is planned again.
A cleared field earns a certificate. StrawLink never reports or penalises anyone.

text: Every plant sees how much straw is coming, and when its depot will be full.
For fields no machine reaches, the Air page shows which villages and schools are downwind this afternoon.
We replayed the entire 2025 season, and report it honestly.

text: Most fields burned within two days of harvest. Knowing early matters most, so the forecast and the farmer's message come first.
StrawLink runs entirely on AWS.

text: The satellite signals, roads and planner are real. The fleet and plants are synthetic today, one config file away from a real block.
Clear this one block in time, and up to nine and a half tonnes of fine particles never reach the air.
StrawLink. Every field cleared in time, so no one has to burn.
